actor.name: National Unity Government and People's Defence Forces

stances.note: National Unity Government and People's Defence Forces has not written its reading of Myanmar; the atlas mirrors Myanmar's 'adversary' reading as 'adversary' at low confidence, on the same evidence. Bond and trend are not assessed from this side.

sources.title: Myanmar Junta Declares National Unity Government, CRPH, Defense Forces as Terrorist Groups
Myanmar junta designates shadow government as a terrorist group (AFP)

stances_toward.note: The one mortal enemy on the card (review addition). On 8 May 2021 the junta's Anti-Terrorism Central Committee declared the National Unity Government, the CRPH and the newly formed People's Defence Force terrorist organisations under the 2014 Counter-Terrorism Law, after first listing them as unlawful associations with contact treated as high treason; the resistance's declared aim is the end of military rule, the junta's is their destruction, so adversary in the atlas's sense (the EAOs with truces, like the Arakan Army, stay rival). Bond grievance.

relations_to.summary: State of the war: the army's stable control is put at 72-220 of 330 townships (Wikipedia index), resistance forces captured 96 towns by 1 Dec 2025 including 15 district-level, the army has retaken bases outside Bhamo, DW reads 2026 as a stalemate with the army regaining ground; the army declared a ceasefire from 2 to 22 Apr 2025 after the 28 Mar earthquake; conscription is estimated at about 120,000 draftees.
relations_to.note: Conscription law of 2024 (People's Military Service Law) is the brief's fact; only the ~120,000 estimate was found, in the Wikipedia infobox (tier 4). Gap: a primary source for the law.

sources.title: Myanmar military regains ground amid five-year civil war stalemate
Myanmar military recaptures crucial bases outside Bhamo

relations_to.summary: The election was held in three phases (28 Dec 2025, 11 Jan and 25 Jan 2026; turnout reported at 52%, 55% and 56%) without a vote in 67 townships; opposition groups called a boycott and critics called it a sham; the USDP won 231 lower-house seats and parliament elected Min Aung Hlaing president (sworn in 10 Apr 2026).
relations_to.note: Upper-house count conflicts: DVB reports 56 of 79 seats for the USDP, Wikipedia 108 including proportional seats; only the lower-house figure (231, both sources) is used.
